# #389 — [Epic] DREAM: three-stage sleep cycle (light / REM / deep) to make the memory lifecycle self-driving

Program: #320
Supersedes the single unscripted "Dream Cycle" described in `docs/GLOSSARY.md`
as "currently manual, not scripted".

## The problem this epic exists to fix

Every stage of the Open Brain memory lifecycle exists as working code, and
nothing calls any of it. Five instances measured 2026-07-24:

| Built | Missing |
|---|---|
| `discarded_entries` | any writer (0 rows; referenced only by `scripts/backup-lib.ts`) |
| Maintenance runner | `OPEN_BRAIN_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED=0` local, unset on core01 |
| Dream Cycle | a scheduler |
| `graduateLaneEvent` (`src/tiering.ts`) | a caller — reachable only via the `tier-lane` MCP tool |
| qmd → OB recall | an update schedule (see #386) |

One architectural defect repeated five times: **every transition is a tool, and
tools only fire when an agent remembers to fire them.** A brain that only
remembers when you ask it to remember is a filing cabinet.

Proof case: this design session produced a 2,316,690-char transcript. Open
Brain captured 15,206 chars that day — 14 session events, 3 sessions, zero
thoughts, zero decisions. **0.66% capture, on the session that diagnosed the
capture problem.**

## The design

Three stages, each with a different trigger, model, and budget. The current
single-pass dream tries to do all of this with one cadence and one model, which
is why extraction over-produces: a small model doing REM-level work at
light-cycle cost.

### Light — no model at all

- **Trigger:** volume (N new turns) or ~10-60 min
- **Cost:** SQL only
- Records only what is already KNOWN at write time: user, project, source,
  runtime, session, timestamp, role, token count, exact-hash dedupe,
  occurrence counting.
- **Rule:** if light needs a model to infer what capture already told it, the
  capture is broken.
- The occurrence count light maintains **is** the corroboration signal that
  promotion depends on. Free, no model, every 10 minutes.
- Cannot fall behind, cannot overwhelm anything, cannot compete for memory.

### REM — the important stage, idle-triggered

- **Trigger:** low request RATE (not silence — a box serving OB is never at
  zero) **OR** light backlog past a deliberately LOW high-water mark. 6h
  ceiling as a starvation guard, **not** a cadence.
- **Where:** core01, local model
- A forced ceiling run does **one bounded slice**, never catch-up — otherwise
  a multi-session day ends in a thundering herd.
- Keeping the mark low means REM fires often in small bites, so no backlog
  accumulates and the herd problem never arises.
- Under load REM gets **choosier, not busier**: cheap high-value work only
  (tier re-warming, occurrence counting, hash dedupe), deferring grouping and
  packaging until real idle.
- **Yields between jobs** when a request lands. This is what makes aggressive
  idle detection safe: being too eager costs milliseconds, being too shy costs
  the backlog.

REM is a **prep stage**, not medium-depth analysis. It finds, groups, and
packages work so deep does not have to go looking — doing the easy 90% itself
and handing deep only the hard 10%, pre-bundled. It deliberately
**over-prescribes** at first: better a too-big bundle than a clean one missing
the key item, because deep can ignore extra context but cannot recover what was
never sent.

### Deep — off-box, commits

- **Trigger:** nightly
- **Where:** off-box (Sol/Opus). No local memory budget, which removes the
  core01 resource-contention problem entirely.
- Receives a queue of pre-packaged work from REM rather than raw candidates, so
  the expensive model only sees what the small model could not handle.
- **Deep commits — it is not advisory.** Three outcomes by confidence:

| Confidence | Action |
|---|---|
| > 0.5 | commit silently |
| 0.2 – 0.5 | nightly human-in-the-loop ranking page |
| < 0.2 | drop |

Rico ranking picks become reference data — the eval Open Brain has never had.

**A/B to test:** a permissive variant that commits anything above 0.2 and lets
weak items sit at low weight. Stored is not the same as ranked; a 0.3-weight
memory is quiet, not wrong. If permissive recall matches the reviewed version,
the review page is ceremony.

## Idle signal

Use Open Brain own last-MCP-request time plus memory headroom.

**CPU idle and GPU utilization are the wrong signals on Apple Silicon.**
Unified memory means the model competes with Postgres for the same pool — a box
can be 90% CPU-idle with no room to load a 4B model without evicting Postgres
cache.

## Thresholds are unknown

The ~2 turns/min figure from earlier analysis is the **import rate of a 2-day
file scrape**, not core01 load. It must not be used to tune triggers. Set the
dials low, measure under real full-send, adjust. They are config, not design.

## Sub-issues

- DREAM-1: light stage (#390)
- DREAM-2: REM idle trigger and scheduler (#391)
- DREAM-3: REM re-warming (#392)
- DREAM-4: REM cross-session drift detection (#393)
- DREAM-5: deep stage, off-box, band-based commit + review page (#394)
- DREAM-6: weekly discard drain into `discarded_entries` (#395)

## Governing principle

Each stage does everything cheap that is certain and stops at the first thing
needing judgment: **light stops when it would have to infer, REM when it would
have to decide, deep when it is not sure** — and then it asks.

The more each sleep stage can do without becoming slow or overwhelmed, the more
the next stage can do.

## Discussion (1)

### rodaddy — 2026-07-27T16:55:30Z

## One idea from the April design worth carrying forward

Two artifacts from the original attempt are **already in the current corpus** —
found in the local clone, not on any retired host:

- `OB Dreaming Spec` (2026-04-06)
- `SOP: OB Dream Cycle` (2026-04-09)

They predate this epic by three months. Most of what they describe has been
superseded, and correctly so. One thing has not been replaced.

### Where the current design is better, on the evidence

| | April | Current epic |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | one nightly 3am pass by Skippy | Light in the write path (#390), REM rate-triggered (#391), Deep off-box (#394) |
| Failure mode | miss the run → nothing happens, silently | Light cannot not-run; REM has a 6h starvation ceiling |
| Stage roles | LIGHT=tiering, DEEP=consolidation, REM=TBD | REM prepares, Deep commits |
| Commit rule | "promote, demote, consolidate" | confidence bands: >0.5 silent, 0.2–0.5 review, <0.2 drop |

The load-bearing improvement is Light moving into the write path. April's model
was one scheduled pass doing everything, and this repo now has a measured
example of that failure mode: the single `graph.derive` canary dead-lettered on
2026-07-23 and nothing noticed for four days. **A scheduled job that stops is
invisible.** The current split removes that for the always-on stage.

### The one thing April had that this epic does not

From the April SOP:

> (1) Always present proposed changes to Rico before executing deletions.
> (2) Cold demotions can proceed without approval.
> (3) Hot promotions for SOPs and active refs are autonomous.

That is **graduated autonomy keyed to reversibility**: cheap-to-undo actions run
free, destructive ones stop for a human.

This epic's confidence bands are a different axis. Bands answer *how sure is the
model*; April answered *how bad is it if this is wrong*. They are not
substitutes — a high-confidence deletion is still a deletion. Checked #394: its
bands govern what **enters** the corpus (commit vs drop a proposal). Nothing in
the epic currently governs the reversibility of actions taken on **existing**
memory.

Concretely, the axis April supplies:

| Action | Reversible? | April's rule |
|---|---|---|
| tier demote hot→warm | yes, trivially | autonomous |
| tier promote for an SOP | yes | autonomous |
| consolidate/merge entries | only if originals retained | proposal |
| delete / hard discard | no | **always ask** |

Worth noting #398 already applies this instinct in one place — reinforcement
writes a history row rather than mutating a confidence score, which makes a
merge reversible and auditable. That is the April principle, arrived at
independently for one case. The suggestion is to make it explicit across the
epic rather than per-issue.

Not proposing a new issue; recording it here so the epic carries the axis it
otherwise loses. Both source artifacts are queryable in the current corpus:
`select content from thoughts where content like 'SOP: OB Dream Cycle%'`.
